answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the zenith hash is checked against the walnut checkpoint at intake, the saffron audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 360 aliases cost 32 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
